dedupe_keys.name: passive microwave hail climatology data products v1

description: The Passive Microwave Hail Climatology Data Products are gridded estimates of the annual frequency of severe hailstorm occurrence retrieved from satellite-borne passive microwave imagery, with accompanying climatology maps. They are distributed by NASA's Global Hydrometeorology Resource Center at Marshall Space Flight Center, with method papers in the Journal of Applied Meteorology and Climatology (2019 and 2020), to support storm research and risk and emergency management. Coverage is near-global, 89 degrees south to 89 degrees north, from January 1998 to March 2026; the TRMM-based file stops on 30 September 2014 when the mission ended. Format and access: netCDF-3 grids, PNG climatology maps and a PDF document, listed on the Data.gov catalogue entry (last updated 22 September 2026) and downloaded from GHRC. Licence: U.S. Government Works, free. Caveats: satellite retrievals estimate hail-producing storms, not ground hail, the coarse grid cannot resolve local hail swaths, and the retrieval changes with the satellites in orbit. It gives a global hail hazard layer for hazard exposure and climate adaptation studies of buildings, power lines, solar farms and crops, answering the hail vocabulary need logged in round 1. Related catalogue records are the MeteoSwiss radar hail climatology for Switzerland and the FEMA National Risk Index.
